title: The Truth
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji left the core of the Heavenly Secrets Eye with his awakening mission, what he didn't know was—something was slowly awakening within the remnants of that ten-thousand-year-old existence.

text.content: The moment he stepped through the Forbidden Gate, heaven and earth spun. Chen Ji felt himself plunging into an endless darkness, wind howling past his ears, yet nothing visible before his eyes. How long passed—perhaps three breaths, perhaps eternity—before his feet finally touched solid ground. Opening his eyes, what met his gaze was a vast, boundless void. Countless points of light floated like stars, each faintly revealing humanoid silhouettes within, like insects trapped in amber. Chen Ji's pupils contracted: the Tianji Record Fragment had automatically surfaced in his palm at this moment, glowing faintly, as if responding to something.

In the deepest part of the Void, a massive Eye slowly opened. Its size was enough to devour stars; its gaze, so profound it seemed condensed with the vicissitudes of myriad ages. It had no physical form—merely a projection of will beyond the mortal realm—yet it caused Chen Ji to feel a bone-deep chill surge from the soles of his feet straight to his crown. This was the Heavenly Secrets Eye. Cold sweat seeped from Chen Ji's palm, but his gaze was unexpectedly calm. He had seen too many enemies, too many conspiracies, and had long learned to remain composed in any circumstance. That Eye regarded him, as if looking at an ant, yet also as if gazing upon a guest it had long awaited.

dialogue.content: "You've finally arrived." The voice came from all directions, ancient, majestic, yet devoid of any emotion, like immutable laws themselves. The Heavenly Secrets Eye's projection slowly drew nearer, its gaze sweeping over Chen Ji. "Inheritor of the Tianji Record... I've waited for you a long time." Chen Ji stood with hands clasped, his voice steady: "Since the senior called, Chen Ji dared not refuse. But I wonder—for how long has the senior been waiting?" "Three thousand years." The Heavenly Secrets Eye's voice carried nofluctuation. "From the day the last Prophet died."

text.content: Three thousand years. Chen Ji silently repeated the number, revealing nothing on his face. He surveyed his surroundings, looking at those figures imprisoned within the light specks, and suddenly asked: "What are all these?" "Chess pieces." The Heavenly Secrets Eye replied without evasion. "Prophets through the ages, cultivators who attempted to peer into Heavenly Secrets, mortals drawn into the chess game... They are all 'fuel' I use to maintain this realm's operation." Chen Ji's fingertips grew cold. These light specks numbered in the tens of millions? Behind each one lay a living life, a shattered family. This was Heaven's Way. Cold, efficient, utterly merciless.

"You wish to know the truth?" As if seeing through Chen Ji's thoughts, the Heavenly Secrets Eye said, "Very well, I'll let you see." The Void twisted abruptly, and scenes unfolded before Chen Ji's eyes—Ten thousand years ago, an existence radiating dazzling brilliance walked alone toward the source of the Heavenly Secrets Eye. Its form was majestic as a mountain, its aura vast as the galaxy, step by step approaching the ultimate forbidden place. That was... the true bearing of an Immortal. Chen Ji held his breath, staring at that figure. In the vision, that existence stretched out its hand, as if to tear something apart—Then, everything stopped abruptly.

At the edge of the Void, Chen Ji finally saw that remnant. It floated in endless darkness, form similar to a human yet emanating a despair that chilled the heart. Its chest bore a massive hole, edges scorched black, as if blasted through by some tremendous force. Even after ten thousand years of death, that unwilling obsession still lingered, forming a faint halo around the remnant. "Its name is Pangu." The Heavenly Secrets Eye's voice sounded. "Thirty thousand years ago, it was the existence closest to 'breaking the game' that I have ever witnessed. It discovered the truth and attempted to shatter the board—" Chen Ji interjected: "And then failed." "No." The Heavenly Secrets Eye's voice suddenly turned strange. "It succeeded. It truly shattered one corner of the board—but beyond that board, there lies an even greater board."

dialogue.content: "You mean to say..." Chen Ji's voice slightly rasped, "you are not the ultimate?" The Heavenly Secrets Eye fell silent for a moment, and something like... fear? flickered in that massive gaze. "I am a chess piece." Its voice no longer carried majesty, but rather a hint of weariness. "You thought the Heavenly Secrets Eye was the supreme will of this realm? No. I am merely a chess piece placed by 'that One' in this celestial domain. The Tianji Record you compete for, the Prophet's abilities, the so-called Heavenly Fate—merely tools for that One's boredom." Lightning flashed in Chen Ji's mind, countless fragments suddenly connecting. "So, defeating you... is meaningless."

text.content: "Correct." The Heavenly Secrets Eye's voice carried a trace of mockery, yet also a hint of relief. "Even if you kill me, another puppet takes the throne. The true enemy has never been on the board—but in the heart of the one who moves the pieces." Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, his mind racing. If the Heavenly Secrets Eye was merely a chess piece, then who was the true enemy? What did that "higher existence" want? Why arrange all this? Suddenly, the Tianji Record Fragment violently trembled, and a beam of light shot forth, condensing into a blurry figure before Chen Ji. It was Mo Xiansheng! The guardian in remnant soul form appeared proactively for the first time, his features even more illusory than before, as if he might dissipate at any moment.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji." Mo Xiansheng's voice was aged yet urgent. "Time is running out; I can only tell you the crucial parts." His illusory form drifted toward Chen Ji. "The method to break the game is not to kill any chess piece—but to awaken all the chess pieces." "Awaken?" "Those beings within the light specks are not truly extinguished." Mo Xiansheng's voice quickened. "Their consciousness is suppressed, their memories sealed, becoming energy that maintains the board's operation. Only by making them 'awaken,' realize the truth of their manipulation—the board will lose its meaning." Chen Ji's heart shuddered: "So the key is not battle, but..." "Spreading the truth." Mo Xiansheng's form began to flicker. "Let every person know they are chess pieces, let every piece rebel—this is precisely what that existence fears most."

text.content:
Before the words could finish, Mo Xiansheng's figure suddenly dimmed, as if severed by some force.

"No—" Chen Ji reached out, only to grasp at emptiness.

At the same time, among the countless points of light, a faint yet familiar glow suddenly flickered to life.

Chen Ji spun his head sharply, his pupils contracting.

Within that light, the silhouette of a young girl was faintly visible. Her face was haggard, her eyes tightly closed, and a sinister rune pulsed at her brow center.

It was Chen Nian!

His younger sister, the one taken by the Holy Sect to serve as the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key,' had been trapped here all along!"

dialogue.content:
"Nian Nian!"

Chen Ji's voice trembled for the first time. He rushed toward that light, only to be pushed back by an invisible force. The Heavenly Eye's cold voice rang out:

"Don't bother. These pieces are all meticulously selected 'cores.' Without my permission, no one can take them away."

Chen Ji stood up, his eyes burning with unprecedented fury. His sister, his flesh and blood, had been imprisoned as a chess piece for who knows how many years!

"What have you done to her?!"

"Me?" The Heavenly Eye's voice carried a hint of innocence. "She came herself. As the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key,' she can naturally interfere with the Tianji Record's foresight—did you think she appeared in your vision by accident?"

Chen Ji froze.

So that was it. Chen Nian had been trying to protect him all along, using her existence to interfere with the Tianji Record's operation, preventing him from being completely seen through by that 'higher existence.'

And he had only learned the truth today.

text.content:
"So, the key to breaking the chess game..." Chen Ji's voice was low but firm. "Is to awaken everyone, including her."

"You're clever." The Heavenly Eye's voice returned to its coldness. "But do you know what this means? Awakening all the pieces equals completely tearing face with that existence. He will act personally—and you are merely a small cultivator who just stepped onto the immortal path."

Chen Ji slowly turned around, facing that colossal eye.

He thought of the years of endurance and planning beneath histrash appearance. He thought of Su Qingyao's trust, Ye Qing's cooperation, Han Lie's obsession, Ling Yuan's ambition. He thought of every life drawn into the chess game, every soul struggling in darkness.

He smiled.

"I, Chen Ji, have never been someone who only looks at combat power."

text.content: "That existence... what does he want?" Chen Ji's voice was calm yet sharp. "If it's just for entertainment, why bother setting up such a massive chess game?"
The Heavenly Eye's gaze flickered slightly, seemingly hesitating whether to answer this question.

At this moment, the space of the Heavenly Eye suddenly trembled violently. Those floating points of light began flashing frantically, countless scenes flickering past like a kaleidoscope—

Chen Ji saw Su Qingyao standing alone in the Tianqing Sect, facing Ling Yuan's interrogation. He saw Ye Qing driven into a corner in the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path. He saw Han Lie confronting a group of mysterious black-robed figures.

"They are restless." The Heavenly Eye's voice turned ice-cold. "Your arrival has caused too great a shock. These chess pieces... are beginning to awaken somewhat."

Chen Ji's heart stirred. The radiance of the Tianji Record Fragment was growing stronger—not merely his power, but a resonance of countless suppressed consciousnesses.

The flame of awakening had been ignited.

dialogue.content:
"You know," the Heavenly Eye suddenly spoke, its voice carrying a hint of complex emotion, "before Pangu died, he uttered a single phrase. He said: 'The day chess pieces awaken is the day the chess player falls.'"

That colossal eye slowly closed, then slowly opened.

"I have waited thirty thousand years—not for another Pangu, but for someone capable of awakening all chess pieces simultaneously."

Chen Ji shuddered throughout his body: "You... have been waiting for this opportunity?"

"I am a chess piece," the Heavenly Eye's voice resonated deeply, "but also a sentient being. Having been wielded as a tool for thirty millennia, don't you think I harbor resentment?"

text.content:
In this moment, Chen Ji suddenly understood.

The Heavenly Eye was not an absolute enemy. It was a puppet controlled by higher existences, yet also a being with self-awareness. Thirty thousand years of imprisonment, thirty thousand years of waiting—it sought an opportunity.

An opportunity to shatter the chessboard.

"Therefore, you will assist me?" Chen Ji asked.

"Not assisting you." The Heavenly Eye's voice regained its cold detachment. "Assisting myself. You awaken the chess pieces, and I loosen the cracks in the chessboard at critical moments."

"And the price?"

"When you truly break the chessboard," the Heavenly Eye's voice carried a hint of amusement, "I want that 'higher existence's' life."

Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then extended his hand.

"Deal."

The Heavenly Eye's gaze slightly constricted, seemingly unprepared for his swift agreement. Immediately, a hint of amusement spread across that gaze.

"Excellent. You possess more resolve than I anticipated."

A beam of light shot from the Heavenly Eye, landing in Chen Ji's palm. Within that radiance dwelled a fragment of... consciousness?

"This represents my complete understanding of that existence." The Heavenly Eye's voice turned solemn. "Including his weaknesses, his objectives, and... what he fears most."

Chen Ji firmly grasped that light, sensing an overwhelming torrent of information flooding his mind.

He glimpsed: higher dimensions, endless chessboards, and a solitary figure seated within, holding black and white pieces, playing against the void.

"Brother... brother?" A fragile voice echoed in Chen Ji's mind, brimming with disbelief and joy. "Is that you?"

Dozens of consciousness streams burst forth from the light points, coalescing into a blurry silhouette in the void. That figure slightly bowed to Chen Ji: "Thank you, benefactor, for the enlightenment."

text.content: "You speak true." The Heavenly Eye expressed agreement. "The chess game outside is already arranged—you need to return to continue moving your pieces."
A powerful force propelled Chen Ji from the Void. When he opened his eyes again, he found himself on the other side of the Forbidden Door, clutching a glowing page in his hand... a contract?

As Chen Ji contemplated his next move, the Tianji Record Fragment suddenly trembled violently. A message directly flooded his consciousness - Mo Xiansheng's final words:

"Chen Ji, by the time you hear this, I have already dissipated. But my mission is complete - I have guarded the Tianji Record for three thousand years, only to wait for someone who could break the Chess Game."

"Remember, the key to awakening lies not in power, but in consciousness. When you make enough pieces realize they are pieces, that existence will lose its source of power."

"Additionally, beware of Ling Yuan. He is not merely a piece of the Heavenly Eye - he has another identity."

The voice cut off abruptly, Mo Xiansheng's presence completely vanished.

Chen Ji clenched his fist, heart filled with both sorrow and determination.

He owed this remnant soul guardian a debt. Now, he must complete Mo Xiansheng's unfinished mission.

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, casting one final glance at that void.

"Heavenly Eye, we each take what we need. But I need to make one thing clear beforehand -" His voice turned ice-cold, "If you dare lay a hand on anyone close to me during this process, even just one person, I will毫不hesitated地引爆天机录，让所有棋子与你同归于尽。"

That colossal eye gazed at him, and after a moment of silence, let out a low, guttural laugh.

"Rest assured. I waited thirty thousand years, not to turn against you at such a time."

"However," the Heavenly Eye's voice suddenly turned meaningful, "Do you really think Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Han Lie and the others are all innocent people caught up in the Chess Game?"

"What do you mean?"

"Go investigate their relationship with Ling Yuan. You'll find something interesting."

With that, the Heavenly Eye slowly closed, and the Void began to dissipate.

text.content:
When Chen Ji opened his eyes again, he found himself standing outside the Forbidden Door.

Behind him, that ancient stone gate still stood, but no longer leaked any aura, as if everything had been merely an illusion.

But he knew this was no illusion.

The Tianji Record Fragment lay quietly in his palm, bearing a brand-new pattern - the contract mark of the Heavenly Eye.

Meanwhile, deep within Tianqing Sect, Ling Yuan was conversing with a cloaked figure.

"He went in?"

"Yes, master. It's been three days, and he still hasn't emerged."

"Three days..." A strange smile spread across Ling Yuan's face, "Faster than I anticipated. Interesting."

He rose to his feet, gazing into the distance, his eyes flickering with a dangerous light.

"It seems it's time to let him know some truths."

Meanwhile, deep within the forbidden grounds of the Demonic Holy Sect, Ye Qing was staring at a strange compass in her hands. The needle spun wildly before finally pointing in one direction - Tianqing Sect.

"Chen Ji..." she murmured to herself, "What on earth have you discovered?"

At Xuanwu Sect, Han Lie was roaring at the void:

"I refuse to accept this! How does thattrash keep beating me every time?! Why?!"

Behind him, a group of Xuanwu Sect disciples stood frozen in fear. No one dared tell him that in a place they knew nothing about, the Chess Game had quietly shifted.

Chen Ji stood before the Forbidden Door, gazing up at the vast heavens.

He knew an unprecedented storm was approaching. And he had to find the path to truth within this storm.

The path of awakening had only just begun.
